_comment: The constraint system, after Perec's Life A User's Manual. Each list has exactly 5 items. They are dealt over the house's 5 x 5 grid by mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order 5, so every pair of items from two lists meets exactly once. A room receives the values of the grid square where the knight first enters it. 'match' words are searched for in the room's own content to decide whether the constraint is fulfilled. 'hidden' constraints are shown in red, as on the Wauquaire chapter site. Edit freely: keep 5 items per list.

chronology.what: My grandparents buy the land, with two other plots of similar size; they sell the others and keep this one.
My grandfather begins the first major construction. My father, just married, helps with the planning and errands.
The house is built and furnished, and I am born. My birth is tied to the fate of the house.
The last major renovation. The digital floor/house plans are the only remaining trace of the original design.
